title: Consider merging these isinstance calls to isinstance(…, (…)).
summary: Used when multiple consecutive isinstance calls can be merged into one. pylint calls it consider-merging-isinstance.
message_templates: Consider merging these isinstance calls to isinstance({}, ({}))

title: Too many nested blocks (…/…).
summary: Used when a function or a method has too many nested blocks. This makes the code less understandable and maintainable. pylint calls it too-many-nested-blocks.
message_templates: Too many nested blocks ({}/{})

title: The if statement can be replaced with ….
summary: Used when an if statement can be replaced with 'bool(test)'. pylint calls it simplifiable-if-statement.
message_templates: The if statement can be replaced with {}

title: Redefining argument with the local name ….
summary: Used when a local name is redefining an argument, which might suggest a potential error. This is taken in account only for a handful of name binding operations, such as for iteration, with statement assignment and exception handler assignment. pylint calls it redefined-argument-from-local.
message_templates: Redefining argument with the local name {}

title: Unnecessary "…" after "return", ….
summary: Used in order to highlight an unnecessary block of code following an if, or a try/except containing a return statement. As such, it will warn when it encounters an else following a chain of ifs, all of them containing a return statement. pylint calls it no-else-return.
message_templates: Unnecessary "{}" after "return", {}

title: Consider using ternary (…).
summary: Used when one of known pre-python 2.5 ternary syntax is used. pylint calls it consider-using-ternary.
message_templates: Consider using ternary ({})

title: Disallow trailing comma tuple.
summary: In Python, a tuple is actually created by the comma symbol, not by the parentheses. Unfortunately, one can actually create a tuple by misplacing a trailing comma, which can lead to potential weird bugs in your code. You should always use parentheses explicitly for creating a tuple. pylint calls it trailing-comma-tuple.
message_templates: Disallow trailing comma tuple

title: Do not raise StopIteration in generator, use return statement instead.
summary: According to PEP479, the raise of StopIteration to end the loop of a generator may lead to hard to find bugs. This PEP specify that raise StopIteration has to be replaced by a simple return statement. pylint calls it stop-iteration-return.
message_templates: Do not raise StopIteration in generator, use return statement instead

title: Boolean expression may be simplified to ….
summary: Emitted when redundant pre-python 2.5 ternary syntax is used. pylint calls it simplify-boolean-expression.
message_templates: Boolean expression may be simplified to {}

title: Either all return statements in a function should return an expression, or none of them should.
summary: According to PEP8, if any return statement returns an expression, any return statements where no value is returned should explicitly state this as return None, and an explicit return statement should be present at the end of the function (if reachable). pylint calls it inconsistent-return-statements.
message_templates: Either all return statements in a function should return an expression, or none of them should.

title: Useless return at end of function or method.
summary: Emitted when a single "return" or "return None" statement is found at the end of function or method definition. This statement can safely be removed because Python will implicitly return None. pylint calls it useless-return.
message_templates: Useless return at end of function or method

title: Consider using tuple unpacking for swapping variables.
summary: You do not have to use a temporary variable in order to swap variables. Using "tuple unpacking" to directly swap variables makes the intention more clear. pylint calls it consider-swap-variables.
message_templates: Consider using tuple unpacking for swapping variables

title: Consider using str.join(sequence) for concatenating strings from an iterable.
summary: Using str.join(sequence) is faster, uses less memory and increases readability compared to for-loop iteration. pylint calls it consider-using-join.
message_templates: Consider using str.join(sequence) for concatenating strings from an iterable

title: Consider merging these comparisons with 'in' by using '… …in (…)'. Use a set instead if elements are hashable.
summary: To check if a variable is equal to one of many values, combine the values into a set or tuple and check if the variable is contained "in" it instead of checking for equality against each of the values. This is faster and less verbose. pylint calls it consider-using-in.
message_templates: Consider merging these comparisons with 'in' by using '{} {}in ({})'. Use a set instead if elements are hashable.

title: Consider using dict.get for getting values from a dict if a key is present or a default if not.
summary: Using the builtin dict.get for getting a value from a dictionary if a key is present or a default if not, is simpler and considered more idiomatic, although sometimes a bit slower. pylint calls it consider-using-get.
message_templates: Consider using dict.get for getting values from a dict if a key is present or a default if not

title: Simplify chained comparison between the operands: ….
summary: This message is emitted when pylint encounters boolean operation like "a < b and b < c", suggesting instead to refactor it to "a < b < c". pylint calls it chained-comparison.
message_templates: Simplify chained comparison between the operands: {}

title: Consider using a dictionary comprehension.
summary: Emitted when we detect the creation of a dictionary using the dict() callable and a transient list. Although there is nothing syntactically wrong with this code, it is hard to read and can be simplified to a dict comprehension. Also it is faster since you don't need to create another transient list. pylint calls it consider-using-dict-comprehension.
message_templates: Consider using a dictionary comprehension

title: Consider using a set comprehension.
summary: Although there is nothing syntactically wrong with this code, it is hard to read and can be simplified to a set comprehension. Also it is faster since you don't need to create another transient list. pylint calls it consider-using-set-comprehension.
message_templates: Consider using a set comprehension

title: The if expression can be replaced with ….
summary: Used when an if expression can be replaced with 'bool(test)' or simply 'test' if the boolean cast is implicit. pylint calls it simplifiable-if-expression.
message_templates: The if expression can be replaced with {}

title: Unnecessary "…" after "raise", ….
summary: Used in order to highlight an unnecessary block of code following an if, or a try/except containing a raise statement. As such, it will warn when it encounters an else following a chain of ifs, all of them containing a raise statement. pylint calls it no-else-raise.
message_templates: Unnecessary "{}" after "raise", {}

title: Unnecessary use of a comprehension, use … instead.
summary: Instead of using an identity comprehension, consider using the list, dict or set constructor. It is faster and simpler. pylint calls it unnecessary-comprehension.
message_templates: Unnecessary use of a comprehension, use {} instead.

title: Consider using 'sys.exit' instead.
summary: Contrary to 'exit()' or 'quit()', 'sys.exit' does not rely on the site module being available (as the 'sys' module is always available). pylint calls it consider-using-sys-exit.
message_templates: Consider using 'sys.exit' instead

title: Unnecessary "…" after "break", ….
summary: Used in order to highlight an unnecessary block of code following an if containing a break statement. As such, it will warn when it encounters an else following a chain of ifs, all of them containing a break statement. pylint calls it no-else-break.
message_templates: Unnecessary "{}" after "break", {}

title: Unnecessary "…" after "continue", ….
summary: Used in order to highlight an unnecessary block of code following an if containing a continue statement. As such, it will warn when it encounters an else following a chain of ifs, all of them containing a continue statement. pylint calls it no-else-continue.
message_templates: Unnecessary "{}" after "continue", {}

title: Consider using Python 3 style super() without arguments.
summary: Emitted when calling the super() builtin with the current class and instance. On Python 3 these arguments are the default and they can be omitted. pylint calls it super-with-arguments.
message_templates: Consider using Python 3 style super() without arguments

title: Boolean condition "…" may be simplified to "…".
summary: Emitted when a boolean condition is able to be simplified. pylint calls it simplifiable-condition.
message_templates: Boolean condition "{}" may be simplified to "{}"

title: Boolean condition '…' will always evaluate to '…'.
summary: Emitted when a boolean condition can be simplified to a constant value. pylint calls it condition-evals-to-constant.
message_templates: Boolean condition '{}' will always evaluate to '{}'

title: Consider using a generator instead '…(…)'.
summary: If your container can be large using a generator will bring better performance. pylint calls it consider-using-generator.
message_templates: Consider using a generator instead '{}({})'

title: Use a generator instead '…(…)'.
summary: Comprehension inside of 'any', 'all', 'max', 'min' or 'sum' is unnecessary. A generator would be sufficient and faster. pylint calls it use-a-generator.
message_templates: Use a generator instead '{}({})'

title: Consider using '…' instead of unnecessary if block.
summary: Using the min builtin instead of a conditional improves readability and conciseness. pylint calls it consider-using-min-builtin.
message_templates: Consider using '{}' instead of unnecessary if block

title: Consider using '…' instead of unnecessary if block.
summary: Using the max builtin instead of a conditional improves readability and conciseness. pylint calls it consider-using-max-builtin.
message_templates: Consider using '{}' instead of unnecessary if block

title: Consider using 'with' for resource-allocating operations.
summary: Emitted if a resource-allocating assignment or call may be replaced by a 'with' block. By using 'with' the release of the allocated resources is ensured even in the case of an exception. pylint calls it consider-using-with.
message_templates: Consider using 'with' for resource-allocating operations

title: Unnecessary dictionary index lookup, use '…' instead.
summary: Emitted when iterating over the dictionary items (key-item pairs) and accessing the value by index lookup. The value can be accessed directly instead. pylint calls it unnecessary-dict-index-lookup.
message_templates: Unnecessary dictionary index lookup, use '{}' instead

title: Consider using [] instead of list().
summary: Emitted when using list() to create an empty list instead of the literal []. The literal is faster as it avoids an additional function call. pylint calls it use-list-literal.
message_templates: Consider using [] instead of list()

title: Consider using '…' instead of a call to 'dict'.
summary: Emitted when using dict() to create a dictionary instead of a literal '{ ... }'. The literal is faster as it avoids an additional function call. pylint calls it use-dict-literal.
message_templates: Consider using '{}' instead of a call to 'dict'.

title: Unnecessary list index lookup, use '…' instead.
summary: Emitted when iterating over an enumeration and accessing the value by index lookup. The value can be accessed directly instead. pylint calls it unnecessary-list-index-lookup.
message_templates: Unnecessary list index lookup, use '{}' instead

title: Use 'yield from' directly instead of yielding each element one by one.
summary: Yielding directly from the iterator is faster and arguably cleaner code than yielding each element one by one in the loop. pylint calls it use-yield-from.
message_templates: Use 'yield from' directly instead of yielding each element one by one

title: Simplify chained comparison cycle to equality between the operands: ….
summary: Emitted when the operands of a boolean condition form a cycle of weak inequalities (<= or >=). The condition is equivalent to checking that all the operands are equal. pylint calls it chained-comparison-all-equal.
message_templates: Simplify chained comparison cycle to equality between the operands: {}

title: This comparison always evaluates to False.
summary: Emitted when a boolean condition contains a chain of comparisons that is logically contradictory and can never be true (e.g. a > b and b > a). pylint calls it impossible-comparison.
message_templates: This comparison always evaluates to False

title: Use '…() as …' instead.
summary: Match class patterns are faster if the name binding happens for the whole pattern and any lookup for __match_args__ can be avoided. pylint calls it match-class-bind-self.
message_templates: Use '{}() as {}' instead

title: Use keyword attributes instead of positional ones (…).
summary: Keyword attributes are more explicit and slightly faster since CPython can skip the __match_args__ lookup. pylint calls it match-class-positional-attributes.
message_templates: Use keyword attributes instead of positional ones ({})
